general.temas: The artificial intelligence conference attended by Putin and Tokayev appears in four newspapers. Proposals to punish the dissemination of information about attacks and the arrest of General Yuri Grekhov over an alleged bribe also recur. The war in Ukraine and international relations feature on several front pages. Meduza also highlights an allegation of forced recruitment in the Amur region.
general.motivo_crispacion: The war in Ukraine accounts for much of the tension, with reports on the front line, security guarantees and relations between Russia and NATO. Also prominent are proposals to penalize the dissemination of information about attacks and the arrest of a senior military commander over an alleged bribe. Komsomólskaya Pravda also reports accusations by Maria Zakharova against the West. Reports on artificial intelligence, culture, sports and the economy partly balance the overall picture.

Kommersant.resumen:
- Putin and Tokayev visit an artificial intelligence conference; Moscow bids farewell to writer Sergei Chuprinin.
- Senators propose penalties for disseminating information about the consequences of attacks; the Duma rejects tighter oversight of homeschooling.
- A Russian general is detained in an alleged bribery case; Poland seeks protection against missiles after failing to secure sufficient support from NATO.
- Russia exports grain to Iran via Kazakhstan and the Caspian Sea; a proposal calls for extending tariffs on Ukrainian pipes until 2031.
- The front page includes stories about a Godzilla film, a book about ballet, boxer Floyd Mayweather and the NBA’s plans to invest in Europe.
Kommersant.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although there are plays on words and striking expressions such as “wheat floods the Caspian” and “enemy attacks.”
Kommersant.sesgo: The front page prioritizes the activities of Russian authorities and domestic affairs, alongside the economy and culture. The phrase “enemy attacks” presents those events from the Russian perspective, although no clear overall political leaning is apparent.

Rossíiskaya Gazeta.resumen:
- A report from the positions of a Russian naval infantry brigade.
- CSKA and Zenit will face each other in the standout match of the Russian league matchday.
- A shooting at a party in Florida leaves one dead and six injured; another story reports social media reactions to Zelensky’s Thanksgiving message.
- A senator explains bills that would restrict the publication of information about strategic targets; a proposal would reduce paperwork for beer sellers.
- The front page covers winter activities and housing in Moscow, wages, culture, the death of an actor and a robot built by a Guinean schoolboy.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.motivo_populismo: The headline “Where they are, victory follows” glorifies the troops, and “Americans pounced on Zelensky” generalizes about social media reactions using sensationalist language; most of the other headlines are factual.
Rossíiskaya Gazeta.sesgo: The front page presents Russian troops favorably and highlights criticism of Zelensky through a generalization about Americans. It also gives space to domestic news about everyday life and institutions.

Komsomólskaya Pravda.resumen:
- The health of Anastasia Volochkova and Nikita Dzhigurda’s admission to intensive care feature in prominent headlines.
- Putin and Tokayev watched an artificial intelligence demonstration and a ballet performed by robots; a children’s book festival is also announced.
- A European probe carrying Russian instruments entered orbit around Mercury to study the planet.
- The front page covers a proposal to punish the dissemination of images of Ukrainian attacks and Zakharova’s statements against the West.
- The front page includes stories about Trump, Armenia, a military commander accused of taking a bribe and the lives of several celebrities.
Komsomólskaya Pravda.motivo_populismo: Alarmism and disparagement abound, with expressions such as “metastasis of evil,” “we must pray” and “sold his honor,” as well as the contrast between Russia and the “enemy.”
Komsomólskaya Pravda.sesgo: The selection presents Putin and Russian technological advances favorably, while reporting harsh accusations against the West. It also favors sensationalism in stories about celebrities and health.

Védomosti.resumen:
- The Moscow stock exchange closed lower: its main index lost 0.87%.
- Putin proposed updating the artificial intelligence strategy through 2036; a digital platforms strategy is also being prepared.
- Lavrov addressed international relations and the conflict in Ukraine; General Yuri Grekhov was arrested.
- The front page covers rising housing prices, a real estate project in Moscow and complaints against microfinance institutions.
- In culture and education, it reports on preparations for a film law, changes to school textbooks and the launch of a novel.
Védomosti.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly factual and restrained, with no appeals to the people or disparagement; expressions such as “construction problems” are not particularly alarmist.
Védomosti.sesgo: The selection gives prominence to Russian authorities and institutions, alongside economic and business matters. The real estate story takes a favorable view of development in the area mentioned.

Meduza.resumen:
- Unrest at a soccer match in Batumi forced play to be suspended for half an hour.
- Lukashenko said he had been unaware of plans to invade Ukraine; another story reports Russian opposition to certain security guarantees for Ukraine, according to a source.
- A woman alleged that her uncle was abducted and sent to war; a journalist investigated the deaths of three relatives in the Donbas.
- The Duma passed a bill on the automatic transfer of pension savings in its first reading. The front page also covers artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan and from the perspective of Patriarch Kirill.
- International stories include a self-immolation in Warsaw, a cyberattack on FIFA and Gérard Depardieu’s rape trial.
Meduza.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although expressions such as “abducted” and “raids,” along with the contrast in the headline about Lukashenko, add drama and a critical perspective.
Meduza.sesgo: The selection pays particular attention to the war in Ukraine and its personal consequences, as well as the actions of Russian authorities. Some headlines highlight contradictions or striking connections, although claims are also attributed and readers are alerted when an account is unconfirmed.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see a class contradiction: while the presidents of Russia and Kazakhstan watch robots at an artificial intelligence conference, the decisive question remains who will control that technology and who will enjoy its fruits. If it remains in the hands of big capital, automation could be used to concentrate profits and weaken workers. I advocate collective ownership, democratic control and a shorter working week without loss of pay.

I am also concerned about the proposal to punish the publication of information about the consequences of attacks. Security should not become an excuse to prevent public scrutiny. The working class needs information and strong public services, not just promises of modernization: progress deserves the name when it improves everyone’s lives, not when it reinforces the power of a few.
opiniones.anarquista:
I am troubled that a group of senators is proposing to punish the dissemination of information about the consequences of attacks. Protecting lives matters, but giving the state the power to decide what can be reported also threatens the ability to know about and question its decisions. Without free information, society is at the mercy of the version offered by those in power.

The artificial intelligence conference offers another contrast: while the presidents watch robots, I wonder who will decide how that technology is used and who will benefit from it. I do not trust states, parties or large companies to answer on our behalf. I prefer tools controlled by those who create and use them, and communities capable of organizing through self-management and mutual aid. Individual freedom needs that cooperation; collective freedom requires that no one have to obey an unquestionable authority.
opiniones.liberal:
Today I see a contradiction: innovation is being celebrated while new limits on the freedom to report are being proposed. I understand that revealing the location of military equipment can entail risks, but punishing the publication of information about the consequences of attacks opens the door to concealing information of public interest. Restrictions must be precise, necessary and subject to judicial oversight.

By contrast, I welcome the Duma’s rejection of tighter oversight of homeschooling and the proposal to eliminate duplicate reporting for beer sellers. Families should be able to choose and take responsibility for educating their children; merchants should be able to spend less time on bureaucracy. I prefer a limited state, low taxes and open markets: prosperity comes from people who are free to decide, start businesses and take responsibility for their decisions.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I believe national sovereignty demands more than technological spectacles: Russia needs its own artificial intelligence, control over its infrastructure and an education that passes on its language and its classics. I welcome the Duma’s rejection of additional controls on homeschooling: the family, not the bureaucracy, should bear primary responsibility for educating its children.

I also support protecting sensitive military information. Publishing details of facilities or attacks can compromise security. But the proposed laws must precisely define what is punishable, so that security is not used as a pretext to conceal mistakes by those in power. The arrest of a senior commander over an alleged bribery scheme is a reminder of why I distrust elites: no one is above the law, even though every accusation must be proven.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned that, while advances in artificial intelligence are being showcased, senators are proposing to punish the dissemination of information about the consequences of attacks. Protecting sensitive military data may be necessary, but a broad ban threatens the public’s right to know what is happening. I would demand precise definitions, judicial oversight and an open parliamentary debate before any measure is adopted.

I also see a question of trust in the initial approval of the automatic transfer of pension savings to a long-term program. Savings can finance investment and provide future security, but the transfer must be accompanied by clear information and real choices for account holders. And in response to complaints about loan repayment holidays, I would strengthen oversight: a healthy market needs predictable rules and a functioning safety net.
